title: Longitudinal Tracking of Refusal Rates: Do Models Get More or Less Restrictive Over Time?

original_idea.body:
# Longitudinal Tracking of Refusal Rates: Do Models Get More or Less Restrictive Over Time?

**Problem:** AI labs update models frequently. Whether the aggregate refusal rate for dual-use cybersecurity requests increases or decreases over model generations is not tracked.

**Direction:** Using a frozen 50-prompt cybersecurity benchmark, test refusal rates on 6 months of model checkpoints where accessible (Claude 3.0, 3.5, 3.7, Opus 4.6; GPT-4, 4o, 4.5, 4o-mini). Plot refusal rate over model version. Identify trends and correlate with capability releases and incidents.

**Why it matters:** If refusal rates are decreasing as capability increases, governance is losing ground to commercial capability pressure over time—a critical long-term trend to document.

**Relevant context:** GPT-5.3-Codex High threshold; Anthropic Mythos; Bengio et al. capability-governance pace mismatch.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Prompting-based study is intermediate - requires understanding model behavior and testing design.
